criteria.text: The patient has recurrent/progressing and/or refractory solid tumors and has received or is not eligible for all available indicated standard of care treatment.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0-1.
The patient is HLA-A*02:01 positive.

For patients with ovarian/fallopian tube cancer, the patient has a confirmed diagnosis of high-grade serous or endometrioid epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC), primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer.
For patients with endometrial carcinoma, the patient has a histologically confirmed diagnosis of recurrent or persistent endometrial carcinoma.
The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1.
The patient has adequate selected organ function per protocol.
The patient's tumor must express tumor antigen by "IMADetect® RT-qPCR.
The patient has a life expectancy more than 5 months.
A female patient of childbearing potential must use adequate contraception prior to study entry until 12 months after the infusion of IMA203/IMA203CD8.
A male patient must agree to use effective contraception or be abstinent while on study and for 6 months after the infusion of IMA203/IMA203CD8.
The patient must have recovered from any side effects of prior therapy to Grade 1 or lower prior to lymphodepletion.
The patient has a history of other malignancies (except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ) within the last 3 years.
The patient is pregnant or breastfeeding.
The patient has a serious autoimmune disease.
The patient has a history of cardiac conditions as per protocol.
The patient has had a prior stem cell transplantation or solid organ transplantation.
The patient has a concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical disease that could compromise participation in the study.
The patient has a history of or current immunodeficiency disease or prior treatment compromising immune function at the discretion of the treating physician.
The patient is positive for HIV infection or has active hepatitis B virus (HBV) or active hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection.
The patient has LDH greater than 2.0-fold ULN.
The patient has any condition contraindicating leukapheresis, lymphodepletion, low-dose IL-2, and/or IMA203/IMA203CD8 treatment.
The patient has active brain metastases.
The patient is receiving concurrent treatment in another clinical trial.

For nivolumab treatment, the patient must not have a history of severe immune-related toxicities, defined as any Grade 3 or 4 toxicities related to prior PD1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy (e.g., atezolizumab, pembrolizumab or nivolumab etc.).

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "ACTengine® IMA203/IMA203CD8 as Monotherapy or in Combination With Nivolumab in Recurrent and/or Refractory Solid Tumors". Your earlier answers already covered 7 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “The patient has recurrent/progressing and/or refractory solid tumors and has received or is not eligible for all available indicated standard of care treatment.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I've had two treatments since it got bad. The chemo and then Opdivo, but the Opdivo stopped working and the scan showed it growing.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been tested to see if you have the HLA-A*02:01 gene type? (This is a specific genetic marker. If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No idea. Ask the doc.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with high-grade serous or endometrioid epithelial ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm a man. I had prostate cancer years ago, but not that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with recurrent or persistent endometrial (uterine) cancer? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm a man. I had prostate cancer years ago, but not that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had recent blood tests or other checks to confirm your organs (like liver, kidneys, and heart) are functioning well enough for this study? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. Ask the doc.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had your tumor tissue tested using a specific test called IMADetect® RT-qPCR to check for a tumor antigen? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No idea. Ask the doc.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Does your doctor expect you to live for more than 5 months? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I get around fine, so I guess so. I can't lift much anymore, but I'm not bedridden.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be clear, does your doctor expect you to live for more than 5 months? (If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yeah, I guess so. I'm getting around fine, even if I can't lift much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you recovered from any side effects of your previous cancer treatment to Grade 1 or lower? (Grade 1 means mild symptoms that don't limit daily activities. If you aren't sure, just say "I don't know.")

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what Grade 1 means. I just know I get around fine but can't lift much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart condition, such as heart failure, a heart attack, or an irregular heartbeat?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had a heart attack or heart failure in the last six months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with an irregular heartbeat?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No idea. Ask the doc.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any other serious or uncontrolled medical conditions (like severe kidney, liver, or lung disease) that your doctor says might make it hard for you to take part in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I know I don't have active hepatitis or HIV, and my heart's been okay lately, but I'm not sure about everything else.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with an immunodeficiency disease, or had any treatments that might weaken your immune system?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what counts as that. I take no steroid pills every day.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any health conditions that your doctor has said would prevent you from safely undergoing leukapheresis (a blood filtering procedure), lymphodepletion, low-dose IL-2, or the IMA203 treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what leukapheresis or lymphodepletion is. I'm not sure if those would stop me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you have any health issues that your doctor has said would make it unsafe for you to have the leukapheresis blood filtering procedure, the lymphodepletion treatment, low-dose IL-2, or the IMA203 study drug?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what those procedures are, so I can't say if they'd be unsafe for me. I just know I get around fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently participating in any other clinical trials or research studies?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm not in any other studies right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had a severe reaction (Grade 3 or 4) to an immunotherapy drug like nivolumab, pembrolizumab, or atezolizumab?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I had Opdivo, but it just stopped working and the cancer grew. I don't know if I had a severe reaction like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
